purpose: Independent practice and summative evidence for B2.5 (equal-group sharing including halves). Captures both whole-quotient and half-quotient share scenarios plus a child-explained reasoning prompt.
student_learning_goal: I can solve equal-group problems with totals up to 10, including problems where each group is a half.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can solve equal-group problems with totals up to 10, including problems where each group is a half.
header.character_watermark: Plus the Pup with a birthday hat in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall).

parts.student_instructions: Share each collection of cookies fairly between the friends. Draw the share onto each plate. Write how many cookies on each plate.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Two share scenes stacked. Scene A: 8 cookies on the left, 4 plates on the right. Scene B: 10 cookies on the left, 5 plates on the right. Below each scene: 'Each plate gets ___ cookies.'

Scene A: a tray with 8 round chocolate-chip cookies on the left, 4 paper plates with light-grey outlines on the right. Scene B: a tray with 10 cookies on the left, 5 paper plates on the right. Each plate ~1.5in diameter.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; two scenes stacked.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P1_TWO_EVEN_SHARES: keywords (cookies, plates, share) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Scene A: 2 cookies on each plate. Scene B: 2 cookies on each plate.

parts.student_instructions: Share each collection of cookies fairly between 2 friends. There will be a leftover. CUT the leftover cookie in HALF and put one half on each plate. Write how many cookies on each plate (use 'and a half').
parts.visual_layout: Middle of the page. Two share scenes stacked. Scene A: 5 cookies on the left, 2 plates on the right. Scene B: 9 cookies on the left, 2 plates on the right. The leftover cookie in each scene shows a pre-drawn dotted half-line. Below each scene: 'Each plate gets ___ and a half cookies.'

Scene A: a tray with 5 cookies (4 whole + 1 with a dotted half-line through the middle) on the left, 2 paper plates on the right. Scene B: a tray with 9 cookies (8 whole + 1 with a dotted half-line) on the left, 2 paper plates on the right. The half-line is a pre-drawn dotted line cutting through the leftover cookie.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; two scenes stacked.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P2_TWO_HALF_SHARES: keywords (cookies, plates, half) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Scene A: 2 and a half cookies on each plate (2 whole + 1 half). Scene B: 4 and a half cookies on each plate (4 whole + 1 half).

parts.student_instructions: Why does Plus sometimes need to cut a cookie in half? Write 1-2 sentences to explain.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank lined area (~7in × 2in) for the child to write 1-2 sentences. Plus the Pup thinking-bubble icon in the top-right corner.

image_placeholders.placement: Bottom of the page; full-width writing area.

parts.answer_key: Open. Accept any plausible reasoning that touches on (a) leftover-when-sharing-equally and (b) halving-makes-it-fair. Examples: 'Plus needs to cut a cookie in half when there's one extra and 2 friends so they both get the same amount.' 'If there is a leftover the share is not fair so we have to cut it in half so each friend gets the same.'

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw your own share scenario on the back: 7 cookies, 4 friends. How would you make this fair? Hint — you might need MORE than just one half!
teacher_notes: Lesson 5 capstone summative worksheet. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Watch for: (a) Part 1 children who draw uneven shares — flag for fair-share reteach; (b) Part 2 children who give the leftover whole to one plate — this is the K-stage answer that B2.5 explicitly targets, flag for the half-share reteach with pre-cut paper cookies; (c) Part 3 children who can't articulate the reason — coaching opportunity for the 'fair-means-equal' explicit principle. Use Parts 1-3 as the summative evidence for B2.5; combine with Lessons 1-4 formative trackers for the full B2.1-B2.5 picture.
